_comment: What carries a charge and bites -- **purely unweathered copper and nothing else**.
Oxide is an insulator, and that is what hands us the decay for free: a run greens over and stops
conducting until it is waxed or a bolt scours it clean (vanilla's own
`LightningBolt.clearCopperOnLightningStrike` walks a connected run doing exactly that).
**Waxed variants are in.** Wax keeps copper bare rather than covering it, which is the whole reason
waxing is the maintenance verb here rather than a way of cheating the rule.
**And so is the lightning rod, because a lightning rod is made of copper** (Jonah, 2026-09-09). That
one line is what makes a rod stood on a pile of arc crystal work with no rule of its own: it is a
conducting mass of one block, driven by the crystal touching it, and `Arcs.reachOfAMast` already says
what a rod on a mass is worth.
**A rod weathers as of 26.2**, where it never used to, so the bare ones are named here and the other
six are left out by the same rule as any other green copper. That is also what keeps a green rod from
throwing an arc: it is not in a mass, so `Arcs.rodsOn` never sees it (Jonah, 2026-09-20).
Spelled out rather than built on `minecraft:copper_blocks`, which would drag every oxidised stage in
with it -- and *which* stage conducts is the mechanic, not an implementation detail.
